title: Pricing Experiment Readout (Q1 2026) — Draft Slide Deck for CRO/CPO Review
body:
Redwood Inference — Pricing Experiment Readout (Q1 2026)
DRAFT SLIDE DECK (text export)
Owners: Product Ops (Chris Osei) + GTM (Soojin Lee)
Review: Jordan Blake (CRO), Evelyn Hart (CPO)
Date: 2026-02-27

=== Slide 1 — Title ===
Pricing & Packaging Experiments (Q1 2026)
Readout + Recommended Packaging + GTM Rollout Plan

Speaker notes:
- Purpose: align CRO/CPO on what we learned so far, what we’re recommending, and what needs to be true (metering + RevRec + Legal + enablement) before rollout.
- This is an experiment readout, not a final pricing sheet. Any externally shared numbers/copy will come from the pricing guidance + Legal-approved language.


=== Slide 2 — Executive summary (what we’re deciding) ===
Decisions needed this week:
1) Proceed with Packaging Variant B as default for self-serve (with guardrails), or extend experiment 2 more weeks.
2) Approve “billed tokens” positioning for Sales + support playbook (tie to new usage API fields).
3) Confirm discount/credits guardrails during rollout (approval matrix + expiry + RevRec treatment).

What we recommend:
- Adopt Variant B for self-serve new customers; keep current plan for existing accounts until renewal/upgrade motion.
- Ship updated in-product plan page + Sales FAQ after metering shadow-compare is stable for 14 days.
- Treat meter-fix period as a segmentation break in analysis; do not mix pre/post in executive KPI comparisons.

Key outcomes (directional):
- Higher activation-to-paid conversion for new self-serve accounts on B, with stable gross margin when cache-hit attribution is included.
- Reduced sales cycle friction in procurement conversations after clarifying retries/caching/token definition (anecdotally strong; quantified via fewer “billing definition” stalls).

Speaker notes:
- There is an explicit dependency on metering integrity. Our readout includes caveats and a confidence rating.


=== Slide 3 — Context: why we ran these experiments ===
Problem statements:
- Confusing plan/overage mechanics created sticker shock and support tickets (“invoice tokens don’t match usage export”).
- Sales had inconsistent language on retries, caching, streaming, tool calls.
- Packaging didn’t map cleanly to common usage patterns (embedding-heavy vs chat-heavy).

Experiment goals:
- Increase conversion and 30-day retention without gross margin regression.
- Reduce billing disputes + time-to-close for sales-led deals.
- Validate willingness-to-pay for predictability (bundles / included usage) vs pure per-token.

Speaker notes:
- Link to “2026q1 pricing experiments overview and guardrails” (Confluence).


=== Slide 4 — Metering & data integrity caveat (must read) ===
Important caveat:
- Metering changes occurred during the experiment window:
  - Fixes for double-counting on retry/fallback for streaming responses
  - Added billed_tokens vs raw_tokens fields + cache-hit attribution
  - Backfills for missing dimensions (e.g., region)

What we did to mitigate:
- Defined “pre-meter-fix” vs “post-meter-fix” segments; primary analysis is post-meter-fix only.
- Excluded days with known late-event backfills and/or drift alerts beyond threshold.
- Used shadow-billing compare outputs to sanity-check deltas.

Risk:
- Absolute revenue deltas pre/post are not cleanly comparable; focus on relative conversion + retention within stable-meter periods.

Speaker notes:
- This is why we’re proposing a gated rollout timeline. Finance (Laura/Emily) wants audit readiness; Product/Eng want confidence.


=== Slide 5 — Experiment design overview (high level) ===
What changed:
- Variant A: current baseline (status quo)
- Variant B: “Included usage + clearer overage” (new self-serve)
- Variant C: “Lower entry price, higher overage” (tested on small cohort)

Cohorts:
- New self-serve signups (primary)
- Existing self-serve accounts (secondary; limited exposure)
- Sales-led pipeline (not a pure A/B; measured as enablement impact + procurement friction)

Primary metrics:
- Activation rate (first successful call + 1+ returning day)
- Conversion to paid within 14 days
- 30-day retention (usage in weeks 3–4)
- ARPU (first 30 days) and Gross margin proxy (GPU cost model + cache-hit attribution)

Stop criteria guardrails:
- Any sustained gross margin regression beyond predefined threshold
- Spike in billing disputes / support tickets related to usage definition

Speaker notes:
- Stop criteria and metric definitions per PM-1848; analysis plan per Product Ops doc.


=== Slide 6 — Topline results (new self-serve) ===
New self-serve (post-meter-fix segment):
- Variant B outperformed baseline on conversion to paid (directional + consistent across weeks).
- Retention: modest improvement for B; C showed more churn among “spiky” workloads.
- ARPU: B slightly higher than baseline; C higher variance (more overage-driven).

Confidence:
- Medium for conversion uplift (consistent trend, adequate sample)
- Medium-low for ARPU and margin (sensitive to model mix + cache attribution)

Speaker notes:
- We are intentionally not putting raw numbers in this draft; final deck will include the exact table after Finance sign-off.
- The “right” narrative is predictability drives conversion, but we need to ensure no revenue leakage via meter edge cases.


=== Slide 7 — Breakdown: who benefited most (segmentation) ===
Segment winners for Variant B:
- “Builder” accounts: steady daily usage, mid-context chat; benefited from included usage and clearer overage expectations.
- Embeddings-first evaluators: better onboarding when embeddings metering is clearly per input token and batch counted correctly.

Segments with weaker response:
- High-throughput integrators with heavy streaming + retries: sensitivity to perceived fairness; required the new “billed tokens” explanation.
- Very small hobbyists: included usage not a strong driver; they remain free-tier heavy.

Speaker notes:
- This aligns with qualitative feedback from sales calls (Acme, Northwind). B reduces anxiety about month-1 spend.


=== Slide 8 — Pricing page / packaging comprehension (qual + proxy) ===
What improved under Variant B:
- Lower “what will I pay?” confusion in onboarding flow.
- Fewer “why are tokens higher than my app saw?” questions when usage UI shows billed_tokens, raw_tokens, cache_hit.

Remaining comprehension gaps:
- Tool calling token attribution (customers assume tool calls are “free” if outputs are structured).
- Streaming partials and disconnect behavior.

Proposed fixes:
- Publish usage FAQ + examples (internal + customer-facing version).
- In-console tooltip: “raw vs billed tokens” and “cache-hit billed behavior”.

Speaker notes:
- SDK and docs work is in flight; aligns with PR-27485 and docs PR.


=== Slide 9 — Margin impact (proxy model; what changed) ===
Gross margin proxy methodology:
- Token-based revenue (billed_tokens * rate by model)
- Cost model using observed GPU-seconds per token by model family + region
- Adjusted for cache-hit attribution (requests partially served from cache)

Findings (directional):
- Variant B appears neutral-to-positive on gross margin vs baseline in post-meter-fix segment.
- Variant C risks margin volatility (more overage + more customer complaints / credits in long tail).

Open question:
- Dedicated attach: if B drives more growth in sustained usage, we should expect higher Dedicated pull-through in month 2–3; not measured yet.

Speaker notes:
- FP&A (Rishi) updating margin assumptions; needs Product confirmation on expected behavior changes after meter fixes.


=== Slide 10 — What we learned (qualitative: sales + support) ===
Themes from customer conversations:
- Procurement/legal: wants explicit definitions for tokens, retries, caching, dispute/credit windows.
- Finance teams at customers want daily exports aligned to timezone and consistent with invoice.
- Engineers want a deterministic “meter spec” and stable idempotency semantics.

Observed GTM impact:
- Fewer late-stage stalls when we lead with a clear usage definition and show “shadow billing compare” posture (we can validate fairness).

Speaker notes:
- This is consistent with ZenChat procurement call notes and support threads re: double-charged retries.


=== Slide 11 — Recommendation: choose Variant B (default for new self-serve) ===
Recommendation:
- Make Variant B the default packaging for NEW self-serve signups, gated by metering readiness.
- Keep existing self-serve customers on current plan until renewal/opt-in (reduce surprise + reduce dispute risk).

Why B:
- Best conversion + retention trend with manageable margin profile.
- Easiest narrative for Sales: “predictable start, clear overage, transparent meters.”
- Operationally feasible: maps cleanly to billed_tokens and usage API.

Speaker notes:
- “Default for new” minimizes change-management and retroactive fairness concerns.


=== Slide 12 — Guardrails (prevent revenue leakage + customer harm) ===
Guardrails to enforce:
- Credits/discounts: follow approval matrix; no ad-hoc extensions without Finance approval.
- Dispute handling: standard dispute window; require usage export evidence and metering incident review.
- Experiment overlap: freeze cohorts; do not reassign cohorts mid-cycle.

Operational controls:
- Shadow-billing compare runs for 14 consecutive days with drift below threshold.
- Meter drift dashboard monitored daily during rollout week.
- Support macros updated with Legal-approved language.

Speaker notes:
- References: discounting policy + legal terms playbook + meter sanity dashboards.


=== Slide 13 — Rollout plan (GTM + Product) ===
Proposed rollout phases:
Phase 0 — Readiness (Week 0)
- Confirm meter sanity KPI thresholds + on-call paging rules
- Finalize customer-facing copy for usage definition + billed tokens
- Train Sales + Support (30-min enablement + FAQ)

Phase 1 — Soft launch (Week 1)
- 10–20% of new self-serve signups see Variant B
- Monitor: conversion, support tickets, meter drift, usage export consistency

Phase 2 — Default launch (Week 2)
- 100% of new self-serve signups
- Begin lifecycle messaging for existing customers: “New plans available” (opt-in)

Phase 3 — Sales-led packaging alignment (Weeks 3–6)
- Update order form templates / rate cards
- Enable AEs to position Dedicated attach triggers (throughput predictability)

Speaker notes:
- Owners: Soojin (GTM messaging), Nikhil (product surface), Finance/Legal for contract language.


=== Slide 14 — Enablement plan (Sales, SE, Support) ===
What Sales/SE needs:
- One-pager: “How tokens are counted (raw vs billed), retries, caching, streaming.”
- Objection handling: fairness + predictability + auditability.
- Guidance on when to recommend Dedicated vs Hosted.

What Support needs:
- Triage checklist for invoice disputes:
  1) confirm timezone + export window
  2) compare usage export vs ledger export
  3) check known incidents / drift alerts
  4) escalate with required artifacts

Speaker notes:
- Sales FAQ tracked in PM-1860; support macros should link to Confluence playbooks.


=== Slide 15 — Legal/contracting alignment (what changes) ===
What Legal needs to approve before external rollout:
- Usage definition language (token definition, retries/fallback, cache-hit attribution)
- Audit/log retention statement (what we retain, access controls)
- Dispute window + credits/refunds policy references

Where the language lives:
- “Usage-based pricing legal terms playbook” clause library
- Standard order form usage exhibit (to be updated)

Speaker notes:
- Sofia/Michael to confirm we’re consistent across MSA, order form, and public-ish docs.


=== Slide 16 — Risks & mitigations ===
Risk 1: Meter regressions create invoice disputes during rollout
- Mitigation: shadow-billing compare gating; alerts; freeze window for month-end close

Risk 2: Confounded experiment conclusions due to meter changes
- Mitigation: strict segmentation; document incident days; treat as separate pre/post cohorts

Risk 3: Customer confusion about caching (“am I paying twice?”)
- Mitigation: transparent usage fields (billed_tokens + cache_hit), examples, and consistent messaging

Risk 4: Discount sprawl during plan transition
- Mitigation: enforce approval matrix; time-bound offers; record exceptions with RevRec notes

Speaker notes:
- These are the four failure modes we keep seeing in Slack threads and support tickets.


=== Slide 17 — What we need from CRO/CPO today ===
CRO (Jordan):
- Confirm: proceed with Variant B for new self-serve + opt-in upgrade motion for existing.
- Confirm: discount guardrails for “launch month” (no bespoke exceptions without CFO sign-off).

CPO (Evelyn):
- Confirm: product scope for in-console plan page + usage tooltips.
- Confirm: “billed tokens” language as standard across docs + console + SDK.

Both:
- Approve: rollout gating criteria and comms plan.

Speaker notes:
- After this meeting: we’ll update the Confluence pricing guidance + publish Sales FAQ + finalize the launch brief.


=== Slide 18 — Appendix: definitions (for internal alignment) ===
Definitions (internal):
- raw_tokens: model tokenization of prompt + completion as observed at runtime
- billed_tokens: tokens billable after applying billing rules (e.g., idempotency/dedupe, retries/fallback handling, cache-hit attribution policy)
- cache_hit: request served partially or fully from prefix/KV cache (field used for attribution + analysis; billing policy must match contract wording)

Analysis windows:
- Pre-meter-fix: before retry double-count fix + billed_tokens field stabilized
- Post-meter-fix: after fixes + monitoring indicates stable drift below threshold

Speaker notes:
- Ensure this matches the Hosted API meter spec in Confluence.


=== Slide 19 — Appendix: open items & owners ===
Open items:
1) Final numbers table + confidence intervals — Sana Farid + Chris Osei (ETA: 2026-03-01)
2) Margin model refresh with updated meter assumptions — Rishi Malhotra (ETA: 2026-03-02)
3) Legal clause alignment for cache/retries/credits — Michael Grant + Sofia Mendes (ETA: 2026-03-04)
4) Sales enablement FAQ v1 — Soojin Lee (ETA: 2026-03-05)
5) Metering readiness gate sign-off (shadow compare + drift SLO) — Logan Wright + Emily Stone (ETA: 2026-03-06)

Speaker notes:
- We should avoid setting an external launch date until items #1–#3 are done.


=== Slide 20 — Backup: notes to self (editorial) ===
- Add 1 slide with an example invoice vs usage export walkthrough (screenshot placeholders; internal only).
- Insert a slide that explicitly states: “No retroactive invoice changes without Finance/Legal approval.”
- Verify that experiment cohorts exclude accounts affected by embeddings batch metering bug window.
- Add a short section on Dedicated attach triggers (when we push Dedicated vs keep Hosted API).
